summary: Two sessions today moved the account from all cash to about 39% invested: DPZ $65 and IDXX $40 in the morning, then VOO $60 and WMT $70 in the afternoon. All four orders filled. I rejected MSCI (pre-open fill into an unpriced earnings reaction, stop anchored to the pre-earnings close, Industrials label to avoid, MCO reporting the next day) and CARG (Technology label and rate sensitivity, invalidation that can't be checked until about February). Both rejections still look right on the information available then. Equity closed at $599.96 (-0.01%) against SPY +0.34%. That one-day gap is noise and doesn't judge the calls. Cutting IDXX from $65 to $40 and VOO from $90 to $60 matched the neutral stance and cut the 10% drop stress loss. The shadow book bought CARG, which I rejected, so that comparison is worth watching over weeks, not one day. The main open question is pace. About $365 (61%) is still idle on day one, and the owner wants the account mostly invested within about a week. I gave a reason for the cash today (neutral stance, mega-cap earnings week, rate-hike odds), but that reason has to expire. Later sessions should add the rest of VOO and top-ranked names outside the avoid sectors, such as VRSN after its 10-22 earnings. One caveat: inputs/learning.json does not exist in this run directory, so I could not apply any Reviewer lessons or check my graded track record. This review does not use them.
lessons: Idle cash needs an expiry, not only a reason. With about 61% in cash after day one, the next sessions should name which proposals fill the gap and when, so caution does not drift into missing the one-week invested target.

Judge DPZ's invalidation against its fill, not the reference close. DPZ filled at 316.58 versus the 305.42 reference, up about 3.7%, so the 274.88 stop sits about 13% below entry rather than the intended 10%. Anchor future stops to the expected fill when a name gaps, as the MSCI rejection already argued.

Resizing for beta worked as intended. Cutting IDXX to $40 kept the book's stress loss low. The defensive tilt (DPZ, WMT, VOO) costs little if tech keeps rotating out, but check it against the shadow book and SPY before concluding it adds value.

Sector-label problems recurred: DPZ is mislabeled as Staples through the wholesale-groceries SIC code, and WMT adds more Staples on top. Cap combined exposure by true business, not just label, and flag mislabels in the thesis when they inflate a sector rank.

inputs/learning.json was missing today. If that file should exist each run, the orchestrator needs to produce it, otherwise the Portfolio Manager decides without the Reviewer's lessons or its own graded record.
